text: example range modeled loosely central Sierra Nevada. long, gradual western slope rises foothills 1000 m crest 3400 m near eastern edge. East crest ground falls away steeply rain shadow. Two river canyons cut western slope, walls steep enough block movement except near heads. Eighty meadows sampled, 12 snowmelt-dependent toads . belong four lineages: West South low elevation either side southern canyon, North East high elevation. Lineages elevation share environment history.  simulation behind genetic data works like . Toads move easily gentle, forested ground. Migrants leave meadow wetter neighbors, drier meadow, stronger pull. warming scenario (+4.2 C), snowpack shrinks share falls elevation, 90% foothills 20% crest, climate projections Yosemite. Low meadows dry , push uphill grows low elevation. task recover pattern genotypes landscape data alone. ex$env ex$env_future hold environmental layers now warming. change meadow moisture largest foothills fades toward crest:

what: Step 1. Genetic differentiation and the direction of migration
title: Full tutorial: from genotypes to a map of genetic range shifts
text: read_genotypes() reads STRUCTURE, GENEPOP, VCF, GenAlEx, FSTAT PLINK files returns allele counts per population. as_popcounts() adegenet vcfR objects. example ships SNPs three formats: Pairwise FST measures differentiation. Directional GST (Sundqvist et al. 2016, diveRsity::divMigrate) estimates relative migration direction hypothetical gene pool shared pair; difference, emigration minus immigration, dM. Positive dM means source sends migrants receives. Ordering matrices lineage shows structure:
code: pc <- read_genotypes(ex$files$structure) pc #> <popcounts> 80 populations, 1318 loci (2 alleles per locus) #>   individuals per population: 8-8 #>   populations: M01, M02, M03, M04, M05, M06, M07, M08 ... pc_vcf <- read_genotypes(ex$files$vcf, pop = ex$files$popmap)   # VCF needs a population map all.equal(pairwise_fst(pc), pairwise_fst(pc_vcf)) #> [1] TRUE fst <- pairwise_fst(pc) dg <- directional_gst(pc) gen <- pairwise_table(fst, dg$dM) head(gen) #>   from  to        fst           dM #> 1  M02 M01 0.16311080  0.038685611 #> 2  M03 M01 0.15357827  0.004226984 #> 3  M04 M01 0.23965549  0.011150260 #> 4  M05 M01 0.08890528 -0.088469572 #> 5  M06 M01 0.22114611  0.013136436 #> 6  M07 M01 0.13162280 -0.027356787 ord <- order(match(ex$sites$lineage, c("North", "East", "West", "South")), ex$sites$elevation) ids <- ex$sites$site[ord] op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 2, 4)) image(t(fst[rev(ids), ids]), axes = FALSE, col = hcl.colors(50, "Inferno"), main = "FST") lim <- max(abs(dg$dM), na.rm = TRUE) image(t(dg$dM[rev(ids), ids]), axes = FALSE, zlim = c(-lim, lim),       col = hcl.colors(50, "Blue-Red 3"), main = "dM (row to column)") par(op)

what: Step 2. Choosing the most likely migration paths
title: Full tutorial: from genotypes to a map of genetic range shifts
text: Corridors start resistance surface. paper, ResistanceGA optimized resistance slope vegetation moisture, eleven blends two compared. example includes components, can . blend, make_transition() builds conductance layer (ridgelines canyon walls resistance 1e6 crossed), gdistance::costDistance() gives cost cheapest route pair meadows. hypothesis ranked mixed model FST (scaled) distance, source destination meadow random effects: Slope-heavy hypotheses fit best: pure slope ranks first, just ahead 80:20 blend simulation used, every path model beats straight-line distance. continue ex$resistance, 80:20 blend, draw least cost paths. Path length measured terrain surface.
code: xy <- st_coordinates(ex$sites); rownames(xy) <- ex$sites$site pairs <- as.data.frame(t(combn(ex$sites$site, 2))); names(pairs) <- c("from", "to") pairs <- pairs[sqrt(rowSums((xy[pairs$from, ] - xy[pairs$to, ])^2)) < 15000, ] nrow(pairs) #> [1] 763  blend <- function(w) {   r <- w * ex$resistance_slope + (1 - w) * ex$resistance_cover   r[ex$resistance_slope >= 1e6] <- 1e6   r } cost_dist <- function(r) {   cd <- as.matrix(gdistance::costDistance(make_transition(r, barrier = 1e6), xy))   dimnames(cd) <- list(rownames(xy), rownames(xy))   cd[cbind(pairs$from, pairs$to)] } weights <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.2) dists <- sapply(weights, function(w) cost_dist(blend(w))) colnames(dists) <- paste0("slope_", weights) dists <- cbind(dists, straight_line = sqrt(rowSums((xy[pairs$from, ] - xy[pairs$to, ])^2))) d <- data.frame(pairs, fst = fst[cbind(pairs$from, pairs$to)], scale(dists)) rank <- sapply(colnames(dists), function(h) {   fit <- lme4::lmer(as.formula(paste("fst ~", h, "+ (1 | from) + (1 | to)")), data = d, REML = FALSE)   c(logLik = as.numeric(logLik(fit)), AIC = AIC(fit)) }) round(t(rank)[order(-rank["logLik", ]), ], 1) #>               logLik     AIC #> slope_1       2289.0 -4568.0 #> slope_0.8     2275.2 -4540.4 #> slope_0.6     2249.4 -4488.9 #> slope_0.4     2214.4 -4418.8 #> slope_0.2     2170.2 -4330.5 #> slope_0       2121.5 -4233.0 #> straight_line 2115.3 -4220.7 tr <- make_transition(ex$resistance, barrier = 1e6) paths <- least_cost_paths(tr, ex$sites, pairs = pairs, dem = ex$dem) paths$fst <- fst[cbind(paths$from, paths$to)] lc <- c(North = "#ff3939", East = "#0070ff", West = "#000000", South = "#4ce600") hill <- shade(terrain(ex$dem * 3, "slope", unit = "radians"), terrain(ex$dem, "aspect", unit = "radians"), 35, 315) plot(hill, col = grey(0:100 / 100), legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE, mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 1),      main = "Least cost paths, colored by FST") pc_col <- hcl.colors(50, "Inferno")[cut(paths$fst, 50)] plot(st_geometry(paths), col = pc_col, lwd = 1.2, add = TRUE) plot(st_geometry(ex$sites), pch = 21, bg = lc[ex$sites$lineage], col = "white", cex = 1.3, add = TRUE)

code: w <- lcc_weights(ex$acc, "M20", "M60", q = c(0.005, 0.02, 0.05)) plot(trim(w), col = hcl.colors(50, "Inferno"), axes = FALSE, nc = 3,      main = c("q = 0.005", "q = 0.02", "q = 0.05")) both <- c(ex$env, ex$env_future) names(both) <- c(names(ex$env), paste0(names(ex$env), "_f")) bands <- list(   lcp_400m = corridor_extract(both, pairs, buffers = path_buffers(paths, 400)[[1]], progress = FALSE),   lcc_0.01 = corridor_extract(both, pairs, acc = ex$acc, q = 0.01, progress = FALSE),   lcc_0.05 = corridor_extract(both, pairs, acc = ex$acc, q = 0.05, progress = FALSE) ) head(bands$lcc_0.05[, 1:6]) #>   from  to snowpack   runoff moisture summer_temp #> 1  M01 M03 404.5949 303.7365 6.580613    26.32584 #> 2  M01 M05 448.9926 327.0718 6.666222    25.87754 #> 3  M01 M06 650.3694 442.9360 6.954292    23.25507 #> 4  M01 M10 463.5224 330.3576 6.692418    25.43482 #> 5  M01 M11 471.0468 337.0674 6.706028    25.53177 #> 6  M01 M16 544.0001 379.0492 6.822005    24.72180

what: Step 4. A bandwidth for each group of features
title: Full tutorial: from genotypes to a map of genetic range shifts
text: Climate may act broad swath landscape, slope matters right along route. select_bandwidth() fits random forest FST feature group bandwidth keeps one lowest cross-validated error.
code: groups <- list(climate = c("snowpack", "runoff", "summer_temp"), wetness = "moisture",                terrain = "slope", cover = "forest") sel <- select_bandwidth(bands, fst[cbind(pairs$from, pairs$to)], groups, num.trees = 300) sel #>      group bandwidth mtry min.node.size       RMSE   Rsquared #> 1  climate  lcp_400m    1             5 0.02672350 0.78889059 #> 2  climate  lcc_0.05    2            10 0.02834149 0.75915926 #> 3  climate  lcc_0.01    2            10 0.02929042 0.74315211 #> 4    cover  lcc_0.05    1            10 0.05683060 0.13809218 #> 5    cover  lcp_400m    1            10 0.05761762 0.10563157 #> 6    cover  lcc_0.01    1            10 0.05814010 0.08152276 #> 7  terrain  lcc_0.05    1            10 0.04135029 0.50222774 #> 8  terrain  lcc_0.01    1            10 0.05159779 0.25553573 #> 9  terrain  lcp_400m    1            10 0.05387279 0.20111673 #> 10 wetness  lcp_400m    1            10 0.05490923 0.16303562 #> 11 wetness  lcc_0.05    1            10 0.05598479 0.15127696 #> 12 wetness  lcc_0.01    1            10 0.05741756 0.12744798 best <- attr(sel, "best") best #>    climate      cover    terrain    wetness  #> "lcp_400m" "lcc_0.05" "lcc_0.05" "lcp_400m"

what: Step 5. Models of FST and dM
title: Full tutorial: from genotypes to a map of genetic range shifts
text: model data hold one row per directed pair. Corridor features directions, both_directions() repeats . site_contrast() adds -site features: difference source destination meadow. Path length lineage effect (lineage_cross(): time since two lineages split, zero within lineage) go . fit_connectivity() runs PCA within feature group, tunes Cubist model (rule-based trees linear model every leaf, extrapolate better random forests), drops collinear features importance, refits.  FST explained mostly corridor features path length, dM mostly contrasts meadows, Yosemite toad:
code: pick <- function(suffix = "") {   out <- pairs   for (g in names(groups)) out[groups[[g]]] <- bands[[best[[g]]]][paste0(groups[[g]], suffix)]   out$path_length <- paths$length   both_directions(out) } now <- pick(); future <- pick("_f") now <- cbind(now, site_contrast(ex$sites, now, env = ex$env)[, -(1:2)]) future <- cbind(future, site_contrast(ex$sites, now, env = ex$env_future)[, -(1:2)]) lin <- st_drop_geometry(ex$sites)[, c("site", "lineage")] now$LineageCross <- future$LineageCross <- lineage_cross(now$from, now$to, lin, ex$lineage_tmrca) y <- gen[match(paste(now$from, now$to), paste(gen$from, gen$to)), ] model_groups <- c(groups, list(climate.at = paste0(groups$climate, ".at"))) m_fst <- fit_connectivity(now, y$fst, model_groups, committees = c(1, 10, 50), neighbors = c(0, 5)) m_dm <- fit_connectivity(now, y$dM, model_groups, committees = c(1, 10, 50), neighbors = c(0, 5)) m_fst #> <corridor_model> Cubist, 50 committees, 5 neighbors #>   12 features after PCA and VIF filtering; CV RMSE 0.01811, R2 0.902 #>   most important: climate_PC2 (100), climate_PC1 (94), path_length (68), slope (66), climate_PC3 (52) m_dm #> <corridor_model> Cubist, 10 committees, 5 neighbors #>   12 features after PCA and VIF filtering; CV RMSE 0.04336, R2 0.532 #>   most important: moisture.at (100), climate.at_PC2 (76), climate_PC2 (59), climate.at_PC1 (57), forest.at (55) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) plot(m_fst$observed, m_fst$cv_pred, pch = 16, col = "#2a7f9e44", xlab = "Observed FST",      ylab = "Cross-validated prediction", main = "FST"); abline(0, 1) plot(m_dm$observed, m_dm$cv_pred, pch = 16, col = "#2a7f9e44", xlab = "Observed dM",      ylab = "Cross-validated prediction", main = "dM"); abline(0, 1) par(op) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 9, 2, 1)) barplot(rev(head(m_fst$importance, 10)), horiz = TRUE, las = 1, cex.names = 0.75,         col = "#2a7f9e", main = "FST", xlab = "Relative importance") barplot(rev(head(m_dm$importance, 10)), horiz = TRUE, las = 1, cex.names = 0.75,         col = "#c8553d", main = "dM", xlab = "Relative importance") par(op)

title: Full tutorial: from genotypes to a map of genetic range shifts
text: predict() projects future climate onto present-day PCA loadings predicts pair now warming. map_pairwise() spreads pair’s change corridor averages overlapping corridors. dM also sums direction vectors, pointing source destination weighted size change, give net direction every cell. plot_shift() draws result: blue change small, red large.  pressure falls lowest meadows. sides canyon, long arrows run east, upslope, foothills; shorten middle elevations vanish near crest, refuge. East crest arrows turn climb back west escarpment. canyons stand gaps corridors cross. pattern built simulation, recovered genotypes landscape data. FST model maps present-day connectivity way. Scaling predicted FST 1 best-connected pair, averaging corridors, shows corridors high flow pinch points :
code: change <- data.frame(from = now$from, to = now$to,                      fst = predict(m_fst, future) - predict(m_fst, now),                      dM = predict(m_dm, future) - predict(m_dm, now)) summary(change[, c("fst", "dM")]) #>       fst                  dM             #>  Min.   :-0.224821   Min.   :-0.3607034   #>  1st Qu.:-0.008467   1st Qu.:-0.0462446   #>  Median : 0.031226   Median : 0.0003446   #>  Mean   : 0.024150   Mean   : 0.0030933   #>  3rd Qu.: 0.054055   3rd Qu.: 0.0455147   #>  Max.   : 0.216369   Max.   : 0.4056813 shift <- map_pairwise(data.frame(change[, 1:2], value = change$dM), ex$acc, ex$sites, progress = FALSE) plot_shift(shift, dem = ex$dem, sites = ex$sites, col_sites = lc[ex$sites$lineage],            main = "Projected shift in net migration", legend_title = "|change in dM|") fst_now <- predict(m_fst, now) conn <- data.frame(from = now$from, to = now$to, value = (max(fst_now) - fst_now) / diff(range(fst_now))) conn_map <- map_pairwise(conn, ex$acc, ex$sites, direction = FALSE, absolute = FALSE, progress = FALSE) plot(hill, col = grey(0:100 / 100), legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE, mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 6),      main = "Present-day connectivity") plot(conn_map$value, col = hcl.colors(50, "Plasma"), alpha = 0.7, add = TRUE,      plg = list(title = "Connectivity")) plot(st_geometry(ex$sites), pch = 21, bg = lc[ex$sites$lineage], col = "white", cex = 1.3, add = TRUE)

title: Migration Corridors and Genetic Range Shifts from Landscape Genetic Data
text: Migration corridors genetic range shifts landscape genetic data. corridoR models genetic connectivity along migration corridors forecasts shifts climate change. implements workflow Maier et al. (2022, Heredity), predicted upslope range shifts Yosemite toad: Genetic distances. Read genotypes STRUCTURE, GENEPOP, VCF, GenAlEx, FSTAT PLINK files (adegenet vcfR objects), compute pairwise FST directional differentiation (dM, net direction migration). Least cost corridors. Widen least cost paths corridors whose cells weighted likely route . Raw environmental features. Summarize raster inside corridor, plus contrast source destination sites. bandwidth feature group. Let climate act broad corridor soil narrow one, chosen cross-validation. Cubist models FST dM, extrapolate future climate better random forests. Maps projected change, arrows showing net direction migration.

Optional leading columns, STRUCTURE's order: label, population (POPDATA), POPFLAG, LOCDATA, PHENOTYPE extra columns. optional first row marker names detected automatically. Alleles may integer codes; missing data -9 default. file marker-name row, number leading columns worked , otherwise set arguments . GENEPOP (.gen, .genepop) Title line, loci one per line comma-separated, Pop separators, name , genotypes rows. Two- three-digit allele codes (detected genotype width), haploid diploid; 0, 00, 000 missing. VCF (.vcf, .vcf.gz) ploidy, phased unphased, biallelic multiallelic. VCF populations, supply pop. FSTAT (.dat) standard header (populations, loci, maximum allele, digits per allele), locus names, population genotype columns. PLINK (.ped .map, .raw --recode ) family ID used population unless pop given. Convert binary .bed files plink --recode VCF first.
